$comment: edikt:artifact type=contract spec=SPEC-013 status=draft reviewed_by=architect. JSON has no comment syntax; this $comment keyword (a real JSON Schema draft-2020-12 keyword, ignored by validators) carries the artifact-status header artifacts.md's other native formats put in a leading comment line.
title: edikt phasea dispatch plan
description: Emitted by `bin/edikt phasea plan` at .edikt/state/phasea/<plan_id>.plan.json. Computed entirely from the stale-sidecar work-list and phasea config — no LLM dispatch happens to produce this file (INV-012). The tier-1 compile skill reads this file and fans out exactly one sidecar-extractor subagent per item, verbatim from the item's own fields. plan_id is content-derived (ADR-020 determinism): identical corpus state and identical phasea config always produce the identical plan_id and identical bytes for this file — no timestamp field exists anywhere in this schema.

schema_version.description: Contract version for this plan file's on-disk shape. Integer, not a semver string — mirrors gov-sidecar.v1's convention (a machine-only v1-or-v2 shape flag), not the PRD/SPEC sidecar's additive-minor semver convention, because this file has no human-authored content to version incrementally.

plan_id.description: Content-derived plan identifier: "pap-" followed by the first 12 hex characters of sha256(created_from.corpus_hash + created_from.config_hash), where the two hashes are concatenated as hex strings (not raw bytes) before hashing. Deliberately carries no timestamp or random component (ADR-020) — the same corpus state under the same phasea config always names the same plan, so re-running `phasea plan` with nothing changed reproduces this exact id and this exact file byte-for-byte.

created_from.description: The two inputs plan_id is derived from, recorded so a reader (or a determinism test) can verify the derivation without recomputing the underlying work-list.

corpus_hash.description: sha256 hex digest of the sorted, newline-joined list of "<item_id> <reason> <artifact_sha256>" for every item this plan would include — i.e. the stale-sidecar work-list as Phase A computes it, before any dispatch. Sorting is by item_id, byte order, so the digest does not depend on filesystem traversal order.

config_hash.description:
sha256 hex digest of the newline-joined string "<phasea.ceiling>
<phasea.force_ceiling>
<phasea.max_attempts_per_item>
<prompt_version>" — the four configuration inputs that change what a rational plan would contain or which contract it is pinned to. A config edit that changes any of these four values produces a new plan_id even when the corpus itself is unchanged. force_ceiling joins phasea.ceiling as a documented input per the SPEC-013 pre-flight correction: without it, editing phasea.force_ceiling from 200 to 500 changed which budget a `--force` plan was checked against while leaving plan_id unchanged — an identical id for two plans with different applied ceilings.

budget.description: The dispatch budget this plan was checked against (AC-018-1). budget.items MUST equal the length of the items array — enforced by the emitting code, not by this schema (JSON Schema draft 2020-12 has no built-in cross-field arithmetic equality check).

items.description: Number of items in this plan. Equal to items.length by construction; a plan is refused rather than emitted when there is nothing to dispatch, so this is never 0 for a plan that was actually written to disk.

ceiling.description: The phasea.ceiling value (config, default 50) in effect when this plan was computed. Recorded so a reader can tell, after the fact, whether a later config change would have changed the refuse/emit outcome. Always recorded, whether or not this is the ceiling `applied_ceiling` names as the one actually checked.

force_ceiling.description: The phasea.force_ceiling value (config, default 200) in effect when this plan was computed — the higher budget `phasea plan --force` is checked against instead of `ceiling`. Always recorded, symmetrically with `ceiling`, whether or not this plan was a forced run, so a reader can see both budgets a plan of this corpus/config state could have been checked against.

applied_ceiling.description: Discriminates which of `ceiling`/`force_ceiling` this plan's item count was actually checked against to produce the refuse/emit decision — "ceiling" for the default automatic path, "force_ceiling" for a `--force` run. Both budget figures are always present in this object; this field says which one governed. Without this discriminator the plan file records a ceiling it may not have been checked against, and a plan computed under `--force` is indistinguishable from one computed under the default path.

items.description: One entry per stale or missing sidecar this plan dispatches. The tier-1 skill fans out exactly one sidecar-extractor subagent per entry, in the order listed or in parallel — order is not semantically significant, concurrency is a tier-1 implementation choice — but the subagent's task prompt is composed ONLY from that entry's own fields (no add/drop/merge/retry/reword). items MUST be serialized in ascending item_id byte order — the same ordering used for corpus_hash's input — so the plan file is byte-identical across runs (SAC-002); dispatch/concurrency order remains a tier-1 choice and is not implied by array order.

item_id.description: The artifact id this item resyncs, e.g. an ADR, invariant, or guideline slug. Same shape idvalidate.ArtifactID already enforces at the dispatch boundary.

artifact_path.description: Path (relative to the project root) of the parent .md artifact this item's sidecar is extracted from — the file the sidecar-extractor subagent reads.

artifact_sha256.description: sha256 hex digest of artifact_path's bytes at plan time — the pinned input. `bin/edikt phasea verify` recomputes this hash at verify time and compares; a mismatch means the artifact changed between planning and dispatch and fails the item as parent-hash-mismatch, never a silent extraction against a version that no longer exists.

reason.description: Why this item is in the plan, mirrored from the real staleness-detector categories in tools/edikt/internal/sidecar/drift.go (Sidecar.IsStale) and tools/edikt/internal/govrun/twophase.go (the bootstrap/missing branch) rather than invented for this schema: "missing" — no sidecar exists yet for this artifact (twophase.go's bootstrap path). "stale-quote-drift" — IsStale found an anchor whose recorded quote no longer matches the parent prose at its recorded line range, including the out-of-range-lines case (drift.go's excerptStale / anchor-out-of-body-length branches, both anchor-drift in effect). "stale-migration-preserved" — the sidecar is a freshly-migrated MigrationPreserved skeleton awaiting its first canonical extraction (drift.go's IsStale, MigrationPreserved != nil branch). There is no schema-version-triggered staleness category in the current detector — a prompt_version bump is handled by the separate, explicitly-forced `gov reextract` path (tools/edikt/internal/reextract/reextract.go), never as an implicit Phase A staleness cause.

agent.description: The locked subagent type the tier-1 skill dispatches for this item. Always this one value — present explicitly (rather than left implicit) so the plan file is a complete, self-describing record of what tier-1 is committed to running, per item.

prompt_version.description: The extractor prompt contract this item is pinned to, resolved from templates/agents/sidecar-extractor.md's frontmatter `prompt_version:` key (tools/edikt/internal/phasea.ResolveExtractorPromptVersion's "vN" format). `phasea plan` MUST refuse to emit any plan (whole-run failure, not a per-item one) when this resolves to UNKNOWN — an unpinned contract is never silently substituted into a plan. This refusal rule is extended by analogy from ADR-055 §4's model-pin rule (ADR-055's text covers only the `model:` pin); SPEC-013 is the first governance artifact to state it explicitly for prompt_version.

expected_output.description: What `bin/edikt phasea verify` checks this item's dispatch against.

path.description: Path (relative to the project root) the sidecar-extractor subagent is expected to write — the co-located <artifact>.edikt.yaml sidecar.

schema.description: The schema the written sidecar must validate against (templates/schemas/gov-sidecar.v2.schema.json).

verify_parent_sha256.description: Documents that this item's verify includes the parent-hash-mismatch check (recomputing artifact_path's sha256 at verify time and comparing to this item's pinned artifact_sha256) as part of proving the extractor read the planned version. This is a VERIFY-TIME check performed by phasea verify against the artifact file on disk — it does NOT require a new field written into the gov-sidecar.v2 YAML itself, which stays additionalProperties:false with no parent-hash key (SP-003: only the dispatch mechanism changes, the sidecar shape does not). Always true; carried as an explicit field rather than left implicit so the plan file states its own verification contract per item.
